evaluation.positioning_hook: A lonely thirtysomething man wishes to be irresistible, gets a 24-hour free trial, and has to choose between effortless attention and the first real connection he’s ever had.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The premise is instantly legible and commercially friendly: a wish gone wrong, romantic stakes, and a clean emotional endpoint. It has broad date-night appeal, though the appeal is more adult and relationship-driven than four-quadrant.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands early and cleanly: David finds a genie bottle, wishes to be irresistible, and discovers the wish expires after 24 hours. The rules are simple, the irony is immediate, and the title concept is easy to pitch in one breath.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: David is a strong lead because his insecurity is specific and his final choice is emotionally legible. Zara and Marcus add texture, but the script is still primarily built around David’s internal shift rather than a deeply expandable ensemble.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The free-trial framing gives a familiar genie premise a fresh, modern hook, and the script commits to a very specific romantic-social experiment. It is not radically subversive, but the angle is clean and ownable.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The wish, the 24-hour pattern, and the eventual cancellation of the deal create a clear engine with escalating discovery. The middle is more observational than plot-heavy, but the countdown structure keeps it moving.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The script turns a classic fantasy bargain into a modern emotional trap: being desired is not the same as being known. That idea is simple enough to land instantly and specific enough to feel fresh.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The city dating ecosystem, coffee shops, bookstore, gym, and gallery give the world a lived-in contemporary texture. Still, the world mostly functions as a stage for the premise rather than a deeply rule-bound ecosystem.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The tone is consistent and lightly comic, with a sincere romantic core and a clean fantasy overlay. The Marcus banter and Zara’s dry authority give it a distinct register without pushing into broad comedy.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: Under the premise is a clear theme about self-worth, performative charm, and the difference between attention and intimacy. The Caroline/Priya contrast and the notepad reveal suggest more emotional depth than the surface wish-comedy initially advertises.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: David/Marcus is a solid anchor, and Zara gives the script a strong supernatural counterpoint. But the supporting relationships are mostly functional around David’s arc rather than generating a truly elastic ensemble engine.

lead_characters.name: David Calloway
lead_characters.demographics: Male, early 30s, contemporary urban professional, straight.
lead_characters.hook: A decent-looking but chronically self-conscious man who has spent years rehearsing charm instead of inhabiting it. He is funny in a defensive way, lonely without being pitiable, and the wish exposes the gap between being wanted and being secure enough to be known.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase lane of Paul Giamatti in Sideways or Jake Gyllenhaal in Nightcrawler before the darkness turns outward: a role built on internal contradiction, awkward comedy, and a late emotional reset that lets an actor play humiliation, vanity, and earned self-respect in one arc.

lead_characters.name: Marcus Green
lead_characters.demographics: Male, early 30s, contemporary urban friend, likely Black.
lead_characters.hook: David’s best friend and the only person in the script who can puncture his self-myth without cruelty. Marcus is the grounded truth-teller, but he is also warm, funny, and smart enough to function as the audience’s pressure valve.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of friend role that gives an actor the scene-stealing rhythm of Mahershala Ali in Moonlight or Lakeith Stanfield in a grounded dramedy: sharp comic timing, emotional intelligence, and the chance to be the smartest person in the room without becoming a lecture.

lead_characters.name: Zara
lead_characters.hook: A genie with dry wit, ancient patience, and a transactional moral code that never becomes cartoonish. She is elegant, amused, and quietly formidable, and the script gives her the rare pleasure of being both mythic and conversational.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that lets an actor do what Tilda Swinton did in Constantine or Cate Blanchett in Thor: Ragnarok—play otherworldly authority with wit, control, and just enough mystery to make every line feel like a choice.

lead_characters.name: Caroline Price
lead_characters.hook: The woman who becomes the story’s emotional proof of concept: intelligent, self-possessed, and interested in David only when he is actually present. She is not written as a prize; she is written as a person with standards, taste, and a clear internal life.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of grounded romantic lead role that gives an actor the understated authority of Michelle Williams in indie romance work: listening, withholding, and then landing the decisive emotional beat without overselling it.

lead_characters.name: Priya Anand
lead_characters.demographics: Female, early 30s, contemporary urban professional, South Asian.
lead_characters.hook: A sharp, self-possessed art-world woman who reads as fully formed the moment she enters. She has enough specificity to feel like a real alternate path for David, even though the script uses her primarily as a contrast point.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actor the crisp, intelligent energy of Ayo Edebiri in a grounded scene partner dynamic: quick wit, self-possession, and the chance to make a small role feel like a fully lived-in person.

lead_characters.name: Miranda
lead_characters.hook: A warm, funny date who becomes one of the script’s early data points in David’s pattern of temporary connection. She is lightly sketched, but she serves the story’s emotional math cleanly.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a compact but playable scene role in the mold of a strong indie date-night supporting turn—something like the grounded charm of Greta Gerwig in a small early-career role, where warmth and timing do the heavy lifting.

lead_characters.name: Jessica
lead_characters.hook: The car-rental clerk whose sudden interest is one of the first visible signs that the wish is working. She is brief, but she helps sell the premise’s immediate social effect.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of quick-hit role that lets an actor make a memorable impression in a single scene, similar to the best of the ‘one-scene spark’ work in romantic comedies where timing and reaction sell the premise.

lead_characters.name: Helen
lead_characters.demographics: Female, mid-40s, married neighbor, contemporary urban resident.
lead_characters.hook: David’s neighbor, who functions as a small but important proof point that the wish is affecting women across contexts, not just dates. She is ordinary, which makes the supernatural effect feel more invasive and real.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a clean character-actor beat role: the kind of brief but specific part that lets an actor ground a fantasy premise with naturalism, similar to the best neighbor/observer turns in elevated studio comedies.

lead_characters.name: Caroline's Bookstore Woman
lead_characters.hook: A bookstore stranger who helps establish the wish’s reach in public spaces. She is more function than arc, but she contributes to the script’s cumulative pattern of attention.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a small but useful showcase for an actor who can make a single beat feel specific and lived-in, the kind of role that benefits from natural timing and an easy, believable presence.

casting_characteristics: One lead carrying the full emotional and comic burden
Multiple supporting women across a range of ages who must each feel distinct
Zara requires a performer with authority, wit, and a supernatural stillness

technical.vfx_details: Smoke emergence for Zara and a few subtle magical transition beats; no large-scale effects or digital environments.
technical.sfx_needs: Practical smoke effect and simple bottle-appearance effect work.

platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model: romantic fantasy with broad streaming and specialty theatrical upside.

budget.note: Contemporary, mostly dialogue-driven, and built around ordinary urban locations with only minor practical magic. The bottle-and-smoke effect is the only notable technical lift.

casting.note: David has to carry awkward comedy, romantic sincerity, and a believable late-blooming self-respect arc, while Zara needs a very specific blend of wit and authority. The supporting women also need to feel individually distinct so the premise does not flatten.

development.note: The central premise is clear, but the script’s commercial value depends on the emotional distinction between being desired and being genuinely known. The Caroline/Priya/Miranda pattern is the key narrative proof point buyers will weigh.

comp_set.title: The Mask of Zorro
comp_set.why_it_comps: A charismatic fantasy-romance built on transformation, wish fulfillment, and a lead whose confidence changes the social temperature around him.

comp_set.title: Bedazzled
comp_set.why_it_comps: The bargain-with-the-supernatural structure and comic wish logic are the closest tonal and commercial neighbor, especially in the way the deal exposes the protagonist’s real need.

comp_set.title: The Big Sick
comp_set.why_it_comps: The script shares that adult-romantic-comedy balance of humor, vulnerability, and emotional honesty, with a lead who has to earn connection rather than simply win it.

comp_set.title: Palm Springs
comp_set.why_it_comps: A high-concept romantic premise that uses a simple supernatural rule to explore commitment, self-knowledge, and the difference between novelty and real intimacy.

audience_target.primary_audience: Adults who like romantic comedies with a fantasy hook and a sincere emotional payoff.
audience_target.demographics: 25-54, slightly female-skewing, urban/suburban, streamer-friendly, date-night audience with appetite for elevated genre.

budget_tier.note: Contemporary locations, a single lead, and only minor practical VFX keep this in indie territory.

types_of_buyers: indie producers looking for a star-driven rom-com swing
buyers building a female- and date-night-friendly genre slate
director-driven companies with a taste for high-concept relationship stories
lane_fit.detail: This sits naturally in the lane where a clean premise, modest budget, and emotionally legible ending can travel on cast and concept. The script is built for buyers who want a commercial hook without needing action scale or franchise machinery.

ip_potential.detail: Standalone feature. The premise resolves cleanly around David’s choice, and there is no clear spinoff vector beyond repeating the same wish mechanic.

strengths.what_it_means: This gives the project a clean buyer-facing elevator pitch and a strong thumbnail for marketing. It is the kind of premise that can get a reader to the next page fast and can be sold to a streamer or indie financier without explanation overload.
strengths.evidence: David wishes to be irresistible, and the wish comes with a 24-hour expiration that turns the fantasy into a trap.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The emotional premise is sharper than the fantasy premise.
strengths.what_it_means: That makes the script more durable than a simple wish-comedy because the real question is identity, not just magic. Buyers looking for elevated genre will respond to a story that can play as both a rom-com and a self-worth movie.
strengths.evidence: David ultimately cancels the wish and chooses to be wanted as himself rather than as a reflex.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Zara gives the fantasy a premium voice.
strengths.what_it_means: A genie who is dry, controlled, and emotionally literate is a strong packaging asset because she prevents the premise from feeling childish. That kind of role can attract a recognizable actor who elevates the whole project.
strengths.evidence: Zara’s deadpan rules, her refusal to over-explain, and her final respect for David’s choice.

strengths.what_it_means: The expiration mechanic gives the movie a natural engine and a clean escalation path without needing expensive set pieces. That is attractive to buyers because the story can move on performance and structure rather than scale.
strengths.evidence: The notepad of names and times proves the pattern and turns the wish into a ticking clock.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The supporting women are used as proof points, not props.
strengths.what_it_means: That helps the script avoid feeling like a one-note male fantasy and broadens its audience appeal. It also gives casting a series of small but distinct roles that can be filled by strong actors.
strengths.evidence: Caroline, Priya, Miranda, Jessica, and Helen each register as different kinds of interest rather than one repeated type.

whats_special.headline: This is a clean, marketable elevated-romance package: a high-concept fantasy hook, a modest contemporary footprint, and a lead role built for a strong actor to carry. The script’s real commercial edge is that it turns wish fulfillment into a story about self-worth, which gives buyers both a clear premise and an emotional payoff.

items.area: The middle is more pattern than escalation.
items.detail: Once the wish starts working, the script spends a long stretch showing variations on the same effect: women noticing David, giving him numbers, and then resetting after 24 hours. That is effective proof-of-concept, but it also means the buying conversation will focus on whether the second half has enough new dramatic information beyond the premise demonstration.

The final romantic payoff depends on Caroline feeling distinct enough from the earlier wish-driven encounters to justify the movie’s emotional landing. Buyers will notice that the script asks one supporting character to become the proof that real connection is possible, which makes her function load-bearing.

She is the most ownable supernatural element in the script, yet she appears in relatively few scenes and mostly serves the rules of the premise. That keeps the budget down, but it also means the most distinctive voice in the movie is not fully exploited on the page.

items.area: The supporting women are intentionally similar in function.
items.detail: Jessica, Claire, Helen, Miranda, and the gym/bookstore women all serve the same narrative purpose: proof that the wish is working. That is clean storytelling, but it narrows the relationship engine and makes the script more dependent on David’s internal arc than on a truly varied ensemble.

issues.headline: The script’s biggest friction is that the premise is so clean it risks feeling repetitive in the middle: once the wish is established, the movie has to keep finding new emotional information inside the same mechanic. The ending lands because it shifts from attention to authenticity, but that payoff makes Caroline and Zara especially load-bearing in a way buyers will notice.
